Rina: Quick report: rotated a project API key and our background worker (spawned via child_process.spawn) kept using the old key. Web server in same process picked up the new key after a health-check restart.

Derek: Most likely the worker inherited env at spawn time. Are you mutating process.env after the worker starts?

Rina: Yep, our rotation hook writes the new token to keyring and updates process.env in the main proc, but the child was started earlier and never restarted.

Anya: Short-term fix: pass the token into spawn options (env: {...process.env, REDWOOD_API_KEY: token}) or send an IPC message to the child to update creds. Longer term: SDK should support a credentialProvider that is called per-request or on stream connect.

Derek: Agreed. Also we have inconsistent env names across repos (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN, RLW_API_KEY). We should standardize and alias old names with deprecation warnings.

Anya: Proposal: precedence = explicit constructor param > REDWOOD_API_KEY (long) > REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN (ephemeral) > ~/.config/redwood/active_session > keyring. SDKs should expose onChange hooks and sampleapps should illustrate safe child-spawn patterns.

infra-bot: Created ticket DEVX-2234: "credential provider + child-process credential patterns + canonical env names" and added checklist.

Rina: Action items: Anya -> draft provider API spec; Derek -> add sampleapp spawn-helper and small README snippet; Ops -> grep repo for RLW_* and open cleanup PR. I'll validate once PRs land. :thumbsup:
